title: Unicode's transliteration rules are Turing-complete
summary: The article demonstrates that Unicode's transliteration rules defined in UTS #35 (Unicode Locale Data Markup Language) are Turing-complete, meaning they can simulate any Turing machine and perform arbitrary computations. This surprising finding shows that a standard designed for text transformation has unexpected computational power equivalent to general-purpose programming languages.
problem_solved: Whether Unicode's transliteration specification has limits on what it can compute
why_valuable: Reveals that a text-processing specification can perform general computation, with implications for security and understanding standard expressiveness
